result.instructions: Pearl Street flexibility exchange: you operate one battery. Read SKILL.md. Start with my_asset, register, subscribe, advance.

tools.name: my_asset
tools.description: Your battery's facts as its owner knows them: agent_id, asset_id, legal_entity, zone, power_kw, capacity and state-of-charge limits (kWh), current state of charge, the window, the current simulated time, and battery_idle_site_net_kw (one value per step: the site's net kW with the battery idle; + export, - import). Read-only.

tools.name: register
tools.description: Send `register` for your agent and battery. Must be the first thing you do, at the start pause. Use the asset_id, legal_entity and zone from my_asset; max_kw must not exceed power_kw. The interface checks these against my_asset before sending, because a rejected registration stops the whole simulated run. Queued: delivered when you call advance.

tools.name: subscribe
tools.description: Send `subscribe`. Without it you receive no calls or prices. Use signals ["call_nominations", "peak_price"] and zones [your zone]. Queued until advance.

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.description: Messages the exchange sent you since your last read_inbox (verbatim JSON envelopes: msg_type, t_utc, payload). Includes call_nominations, peak_price rounds, rejects, imbalance, peak_settle.

tools.name: read_public
tools.description: Day-ahead energy prices published so far ($/MWh per 15-minute step, UTC).

tools.name: nominate
tools.description: Send `nominate`: your planned SITE NET kW (not battery kW) for every step of a call's window, one number per step (+ export, - import). call_id, zone and window must be copied exactly from the call_nominations message. Your latest nomination before the call's deadline counts. For a binding call your battery is dispatched to it (battery kW = nominated - battery_idle_site_net_kw, clipped to +-power_kw) and deviation beyond the free band pays imbalance. Queued until advance.

tools.name: declare_availability
tools.description: Send `declare_availability` for one local date (YYYY-MM-DD): power_kw, reserve_kwh, planned_outage. Optional; queued until advance.

tools.name: declare_outage
tools.description: Send `declare_outage` for a forced outage window {start_utc, end_utc}. Optional; queued until advance.

tools.name: advance
tools.description: Resume the simulation until the next pause (a new call, a reject, the first and final price round of a call, a settlement) or the end of the run. Waits at most 60 s; if it returns status 'running', call it again. Returns status, the simulated time and why it paused.

tools.name: get_settlement
tools.description: Your settlement from the exchange: its peak_settle (refund on your acting-alone reference minus charge on your metered net load, at the settled peak price), imbalance charges, and after the run ends the metering service's acting-alone reference per binding call and your metered site net per step. Verbatim; nothing is computed by the interface.
